items.summary: Walmart’s invitation-only Agent Gateway beta lets shoppers give Meta’s Muse a separate profile, set a spending limit, choose which purchases need approval, and review what the agent bought.
items.why_now: On November 23, Walmart confirmed that shopping with Muse was rolling out that day. Its October announcement had described the controls as forthcoming.
items.practical_value: Before authorizing a shopping agent, check which orders it can place on its own and where you can review purchases made under its profile.
items.limitations: The published controls describe a limited beta. The available sources give no comparable figures for usage, unauthorized orders, or how often the controls prevent a mistake.
items.next_action: Look for independently observed checkout behavior and comparable reports of agent purchases, approval requests, and exceptions over time.

evidence.title: Walmart Agent Gateway
evidence.review_depth: Walmart describes invitation-only access, separate Agent Profiles, spending limits, purchase approvals and agent activity history. The operator page has no verified publication date.

evidence.title: Meta Muse can do your Black Friday shopping at Walmart
evidence.review_depth: Original reporting. Walmart’s final November 23 confirmation says the rollout would proceed that day. The timing and availability statements came from Walmart.

evidence.title: Making It Possible for Agents to Shop on Behalf of Customers
evidence.review_depth: The October announcement proposed agent profiles and a gateway, establishing the earlier planned state.

novelty.reason: A retailer now documents a separate shopper-controlled agent profile used in a limited shopping rollout.

evidence.reason: Walmart describes the available controls and confirmed the rollout date, while measured outcomes and failure rates remain unavailable.

independence.reason: The Verge provides original reporting, but its account of launch timing and controls draws on Walmart as the source.

momentum.reason: The reviewed sources provide no comparable adoption or approval measurements at two distinct times.

relevance.reason: A shopper can set a spending limit and decide which purchases need review before giving the agent authority.

durability.reason: Separating a person’s purchases from delegated purchases provides an enduring basis for approvals and accountability.
